The signal at 1.35 ppm integrates for 10H and shows a dtt (doublet of triplet of triplets) pattern. This is characteristic of CH2 groups in a cyclic system, not CH3 groups. Methyl groups would typically show simpler splitting patterns (singlet, doublet, or triplet) and wouldn't have such complex coupling.

The aromatic signals at 7.24 and 7.41 ppm (4H total) suggest a para-substituted benzene ring.

There don't appear to be any clear methyl group signals in the 1H NMR. Let me check the 13C NMR to confirm this, as methyl carbons would appear in the 10-30 ppm region.
